🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 6)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: unknown (infra-shaped, not code)  •  alerts in group: 2
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin, Vertical App Experience, Transactions` (multi-team — no single team owns the whole picture)   ← inert text per Hard rule #13

Symptoms:
  - DD monitors 302048329 (miurl P95>2s) and 299551623 (ms-search-api P95>2s) both breached severely — miurl peak 56.32s (ratio 27.16x), ms-search-api peak 22.22s (ratio 10.11x) — during a sustained ~29min window (17:36-18:05Z)
  - Confirmed simultaneous with 2 other DD monitors this cycle covering runtime-core-api (RTC, both endpoints, ki-24) and classic/method (ki-2026-07-07) — 4 independent, independently-deployed services, 3 owning teams, all elevated over the identical window per each service's own APM metric series
  - Zero error-log signal on any of the 5 co-firing services (0 status:error DD logs); no CPU saturation (host CPU peak 19.2%, checked); no infra-monitor (Redis/SQL/Mongo/gateway/DNS) co-fire; weak Redis corroboration on runtime-core-api only (4 "Redis operation cancelled" hits, diffuse across 4 accounts)
  - All 5 monitors self-recovered without intervention by ~18:06-18:08Z (~30min total event duration)
  - Two KB false-matches identified and rejected this cycle: "miurl" bare-substring hit a DNS-outage KB (unrelated), "ms-search" bare-substring hit a resolved 2025-01-02 CPU-crash KB (unrelated, and host CPU independently ruled out this occurrence)

Trace IDs: n/a — aggregate p95 monitors carry no per-request trace id; the only sampled request-level detail is on runtime-core-api's Redis-corroboration hits (RequestIds in docs/investigations/2026-07-14-77bdf6b53feea7ae.md), not representative of miurl/ms-search-api specifically

Likely cause: unidentified shared infrastructure dependency (network path, load balancer, DNS, or a datastore/cache shared more broadly than previously scoped) — breadth across 3 differently-owned, differently-stacked services (.NET Core, legacy .NET Framework x2, microservice) makes a single-service code cause unlikely
Suggested next action: joint Admin/VAE/Transactions APM-trace investigation (no single team owns enough of the picture alone); file a defect if a 2nd co-fire of this exact 4-5-service shape occurs
